title: AI-guided design enables E. coli ribosomal proteins without isoleucine
summary: Researchers used computational protein design and generative AI to recode ribosomal proteins in E. coli so they function without isoleucine, then assembled an engineered strain that remained viable and genomically stable over more than 450 laboratory generations. The result shows a reduced amino-acid alphabet can support core translation machinery in this bacterium; the organism still uses isoleucine elsewhere.
ai_technology: Protein design models including ESM2, MSATr, ProteinMPNN and AfDesign
organization: Columbia University, Massachusetts Institute of Technology and Harvard University

evidence.tested: Researchers used computational protein design and generative AI to recode ribosomal proteins in E. coli so they function without isoleucine, then assembled an engineered strain that remained viable and genomically stable over more than 450 laboratory generations.
evidence.unknown: This is not a whole 19-amino-acid organism: isoleucine was eliminated from the engineered ribosomal proteins, while the rest of the cell still uses it. Growth was slower than wild type according to the paper.
evidence.ai_role: The researchers used AI-guided computational design to propose amino-acid substitutions that allowed selected ribosomal proteins to function after removing isoleucine; the strain was assembled and experimentally tested by the team.
